new.title: Tour the Völklingen Ironworks, a UNESCO site
new.desc: The Völklinger Hütte is a blast-furnace complex that produced pig iron from 1873 until 1986. In 1994 it became the first industrial monument in the world on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
new.tip: Open daily except 24, 25 and 31 December; allow three hours. The 45 m viewing platform on the blast furnaces is stair-only, and the Paradies wilderness area on the old coking plant site is worth the detour.

new.title: Walk the Schlossberg caves under Homburg
new.desc: The Schlossberghöhlen are Europe's largest man-made sandstone caves, dug on several levels beneath the Schlossberg above Homburg. About 800 m of the roughly 5 km system is open on guided tours.
new.tip: Tours run on the hour; booking by phone (06841 2064) is advised. Bring a jacket, as it stays cool underground all year.

new.title: Wander the Roman town at Schwarzenacker
new.desc: The Römermuseum Schwarzenacker is an open-air museum on the remains of a Roman vicus of about 2,000 people, inhabited from around the birth of Christ until the Alemanni destroyed it in AD 275. Reconstructed houses and finds sit beside a baroque manor house.
new.tip: Check opening days on the museum site before you go. Combine it with the Schlossberg caves, as both are in Homburg.

new.title: Visit the Celtic princess grave at Reinheim
new.desc: The Europäischer Kulturpark Bliesbruck-Reinheim spans the German-French border. The Celtic princess's grave (c. 400 BC) was excavated in 1954 and reconstructed in 1999, and the French side shows a Roman small town with baths and a basilica.
new.tip: Open mainly April to October; the 2026 exhibition 'Gold im Sand' runs until 31 October. The Roman tavern serves historically inspired dishes.

new.title: Stand beside the Gollenstein menhir
new.desc: The Gollenstein on the Blieskasteler Berg is the tallest menhir in central Europe at about 6.5 m. It is thought to be around 4,000 years old and is the town's emblem.
new.tip: A short walk from the car park; free and open at any time. Combine with the old town and the Orangerie below.

new.title: See the Orangerie, last relic of Blieskastel's palace
new.desc: The Orangerie is the main surviving part of the palace of the Counts von der Leyen, with twelve arches originally. It was restored in 1982-1986 and now hosts concerts and exhibitions; the baroque Schlosskirche with its crypt stands nearby.
new.tip: The exterior is freely visible; check the event calendar for concerts inside.

new.title: Visit Gräfinthal monastery in the Bliesgau
new.desc: Kloster Gräfinthal near Mandelbachtal was founded in the 13th century by a countess of Blieskastel and run by Wilhelmite monks from 1243 until 1785. Benedictines have lived there since 1993, and it is a Marian pilgrimage site with a protected terrace garden.
new.tip: Free to visit; the church is the heart of the site and several Bliesgau trails start from here.

new.title: Stroll the Vauban town square of Saarlouis
new.desc: Saarlouis was laid out by Vauban for Louis XIV in 1680. The Großer Markt, the old parade ground, is framed by plane trees, the Ludwigskirche and the Kommandantur, with a fountain at each corner.
new.tip: Walk from the Deutsches Tor through the hexagonal old town. The market is lively on market days.

new.title: Climb the Saarpolygon on the Duhamel spoil heap
new.desc: The Saarpolygon is a steel arch marking the end of Saar hard-coal mining in 2012, on the Duhamel spoil heap in Ensdorf. About 132 steps lead up to the viewing platform with views over the Saar valley.
new.tip: Free, open at all times; lit after dark. Parking nearby.

new.title: Smell the roses at the Zweibrücken Rosengarten
new.desc: Opened in 1914, the Rosengarten of the 'Rose City' covers over 4.5 hectares with tens of thousands of roses. It is one of the largest rose gardens in Germany.
new.tip: Best in June and July; the Wildrosengarten and Fasanerie are a short drive away.

new.title: Explore the Fasanerie and Tschifflick in Zweibrücken
new.desc: The Fasanerie was the hunting and excursion ground of the Dukes of Zweibrücken. The area holds the Wildrosengarten, a castle ruin, the baroque garden monument Tschifflick and the Trompetenhügel lookout.
new.tip: Walk the Fasanenjagd trail; allow two hours.

new.title: See the ducal Schloss Zweibrücken
new.desc: Schloss Zweibrücken was the residence of the Dukes of Pfalz-Zweibrücken. Rebuilt after the Second World War, it has housed the Oberlandesgericht since 1965.
new.tip: Look at the exterior; it is in use as a court, so the interior is not generally open.

new.title: Visit the Wendalinus Basilica in St. Wendel
new.desc: A late Gothic hall church of the 14th century, the basilica holds the tomb of Saint Wendelin, decorated with the apostles, and is a pilgrimage goal in Saarland.
new.tip: Free; the pilgrim path to Tholey starts here.

new.title: Explore Tholey Abbey, one of Germany's oldest
new.desc: The Benedictine abbey of Tholey goes back to the 8th century. The church and the monks' garden are freely accessible and the Theulegium museum next door covers local history.
new.tip: Visit the abbey shop for monastery products.

new.title: Walk the Celtic ring wall at Otzenhausen
new.desc: The Hunnenring is a Celtic hill fort from about 100 BC with a stone wall once around 10 m high, among the most impressive Celtic fortifications in Europe. A reconstructed Celtic village stands at its foot.
new.tip: Several marked loops start at the Keltenpark; wear sturdy shoes.

new.title: Wander the old ironworks area in Neunkirchen
new.desc: The Altes HüttenAreal holds the disused blast furnaces, the Gebläsehalle and the 1859 Stummsche Reithalle. The Hüttenweg opened in 1991 and the Hüttenpark in 1995.
new.tip: Free access; follow the Hüttenweg information boards.

new.title: See the Salzbrunnen in Sulzbach's salt district
new.desc: The Salzbrunnen house was built over a well that raised brine from about 20 m. Next to the listed Salzhäuser of the old saltworks, its historic rooms host theatre, exhibitions and concerts.
new.tip: Check the cultural programme; the Brennender Berg trail starts nearby.

new.title: Tour the Alte Schmelz in St. Ingbert
new.desc: The Alte Schmelz is a former ironworks of the 18th and 19th centuries in St. Ingbert, with its key buildings listed as monuments and now a cultural venue.
new.tip: Guided tours by appointment via alte-schmelz.org; parking is free.
new.q: Alte Schmelz, Alte Schmelz 64, St. Ingbert

new.title: Swim at the Bostalsee beach at Bosen
new.desc: The Bostalsee near Nohfelden is Saarland's largest leisure lake. Swimming is only allowed in the two fenced beaches, Bosen on the west shore and Gonnesweiler.
new.tip: Last entry is half an hour before closing; buy a day ticket on site.

new.title: Rent a pedal boat on the Bostalsee
new.desc: Boat hire runs from Bosen; in 2025 the last day of the season was 19 October. The lake has paths around the shore.
new.tip: Check the season on bostalsee.de.

new.title: Hike up the Schaumberg near Tholey
new.desc: The Schaumberg is the home mountain of the St. Wendel region with a lookout tower and an adventure park with a barefoot trail.
new.tip: Reward the climb at the Schaumberg Alm.

new.title: Walk the Wendelinus pilgrim path to Tholey
new.desc: The 15 km Wendelinus-Pilgerweg links the Wendalinus Basilica in St. Wendel with the abbey church of Tholey.
new.tip: Allow four hours and plan the way back.

new.title: Walk the Vauban ramparts on the Saar island
new.desc: The Vauban-Insel and the surviving ramparts and ditches are protected remains of the fortress laid out in 1680. The island lies by a side arm of the Saar.
new.tip: Combine it with a stop at the Deutsches Tor.

new.title: Explore the Vauban casemates in Saarlouis
new.desc: The casemates lie along the Anton-Merziger-Ring towards the Vauban island; those under the Deutsches Tor and at the Galerie Kleiner Markt are the best known.
new.tip: Ask the tourist office about guided tours.

new.title: Visit the Neunkirchen Zoo
new.desc: The Neunkircher Zoo, at Zoostraße 25, is the older and larger of Saarland's two zoos and is open 365 days a year.
new.tip: Check opening hours on the zoo site.

new.title: Walk the Schlossberg above Homburg
new.desc: The Schlossberg above Homburg carries the remains of the Hohenburg fortress. A marked Schlossbergtour leads past the ruins, the caves and the viewpoints.
new.tip: Free; there is a car park on the Schlossberg.

new.title: Stroll the Blumengarten and mining history in Bexbach
new.desc: The Blumengarten in Bexbach holds the Saarland mining museum and other attractions of the former Bexbach colliery.
new.tip: Opening times were not confirmed; check before visiting.

new.title: Hike the Natura Trail from Gräfinthal
new.desc: The Natura Trail Mandelbachtal is a roughly 15 km circuit starting at Kloster Gräfinthal through the Bliesgau biosphere reserve, UNESCO-listed in 2009.
new.tip: Plan about four and a half hours.

new.title: Follow the Cerda & Celtoi sculpture trail
new.desc: The Keltischer Skulpturenweg Cerda & Celtoi runs about 6.9 km at the Otzenhausen ring wall.
new.tip: Moderate; start at the Keltenpark.

new.title: Eat the regional menu at Landgenuss Blieskastel
new.desc: Landgenuss, run by the Hämmerle family, has a Michelin Bib Gourmand for regional cooking with produce from the Bliesgau.
new.tip: Book well ahead; try the seasonal regional dishes.

new.title: Taste Karlsberg beer at the Alte Schlosserei in Homburg
new.desc: The Karlsberg brewery, founded in 1878 in Homburg, runs the Alte Schlosserei as its beer venue with a 20-tap system.
new.tip: Try a fresh Karlsberg pils; tours cost extra.

new.title: Eat schnitzel in the 17th-century Felsenmühle
new.desc: The Gasthaus Felsenmühle in St. Wendel occupies a 17th-century mill and serves classic German dishes.
new.tip: Try the schnitzel; open daily 11:00-22:00.

new.title: Have coffee at Café le Journal in St. Wendel
new.desc: A central café in St. Wendel, praised for its atmosphere especially in summer.
new.tip: Sit outside in summer.

new.title: Eat German fare at the Schaumberg Alm
new.desc: A hilltop restaurant at about 569 m on the Schaumberg with a beer-garden setting.
new.tip: Kitchen 11:30-21:00; order a regional dish with the view.

new.title: Dine at Alte Brauerei Grund in Zweibrücken
new.desc: A traditional German restaurant in Niederauerbach with regional dishes, beer and local wine.
new.tip: Open mainly Friday to Sunday; book ahead.

new.title: Eat Palatine and South Tyrolean dishes at Landhaus
new.desc: Restaurant Landhaus in the Fasanerie serves Palatine and South Tyrolean cooking near the woods.
new.tip: Combine with a Fasanerie walk.

new.title: Have vegan breakfast at Altstadtcafé Saarlouis
new.desc: A long-standing café near the old town at Sonnenstraße 14, with vegan breakfast and plant milks.
new.tip: Go for breakfast.

new.title: Dine at Auberge Maréchal Ney in Saarlouis
new.desc: A French-style restaurant named after Saarlouis-born Marshal Ney.
new.tip: Try the French classics.

new.title: Eat Lorraine-style at Alter Bahnhof Völklingen
new.desc: A restaurant with Lorraine-influenced dishes such as a salad Lothringer Art.
new.tip: Try the Lorraine salad.

new.title: Eat home-style at Gaststätte Zum Wildpark
new.desc: A Völklingen inn on Püttlinger Straße with hearty home-style cooking and warm kitchen all day Sunday.
new.tip: Go on Sunday.
new.q: Gaststätte Zum Wildpark, Püttlinger Straße, Völklingen

new.title: Dine at Die Alte Brauerei in St. Ingbert
new.desc: A Michelin-listed restaurant in St. Ingbert in an old brewery building.
new.tip: Book ahead.

new.title: Eat at Pastis Bistro in Saarlouis
new.desc: A French bistro in Saarlouis.
new.tip: Try the French bistro fare.
